rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving means granting a thing's origin, sources, and causes, thereby conveying all its future branches, yields, and fruits, as transferring a garden conveys its harvests.
rows.anchor: Bir şeyin aslını, menba‘ını, esbâb ve illetini vermek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kawthar is abundant good whose sources were eternally decreed for Muhammad, granted at revelation, and includes the causes of future blessings, represented now and guaranteed to continue.
rows.anchor: hakīkat-ı Muhammediye’ye ezelde takdir olunarak i‘tâ emri ile verilmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kawthar as the Prophet's Paradise river signifies the source from which the promised rivers of Paradise flow; Qur'anic descriptions picture its joys as rivers.
rows.anchor: “kevser”in cennette Peygamber’e verilmiş bir nehir olarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mi'raj descriptions of Kawthar as whiter than milk and sweeter than honey, and the community drinking from it at Resurrection, make it the source and superior emblem of Paradise's rivers.
rows.anchor: sütten daha beyaz, baldan daha tatlı ve tînetinden misk-i ezfer çıkar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past-tense promise conveys God's eternal report, present bestowal, and guarantee for the endless future, repeatedly announcing glad tidings to the Prophet and his community.
rows.anchor: buyurulmasında ezelden bir ihbar, hâlde bir inşâ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kawthar encompasses Islam and its supremacy, wisdom, prophethood as mercy, the protected Qur'an, and the many virtues, proofs, rewards, and blessings assigned to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: hakīkat-i Muhammediyeye takdir ve tahsis buyurulan fezâil-i kesîre

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gift's continuing effects include scholars inheriting the prophets, a virtuous community, good descendants and followers, who receive the Prophet's blessing and accompany him beneath the Banner of Praise.
rows.anchor: enbiyâ veresesi olan ulemâ, hayırlı ümmet, hayırlı zürriyet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fā makes the commands consequences of the gift: great benefaction requires gratitude and obedience, and gratitude merits increase; Kawthar also summarizes the preceding suras through al-Ma'un.
rows.anchor: Fâ, sebebiyetle önündeki emirlerin mâkabline terettübünü ifade içindir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer gathers gratitude of heart, tongue, and body, stands at the head of worship, and gives the soul strength through seeking God's help.
rows.anchor: namaz kalben ve lisânen ve bütün a‘zâ-i beden ile yapılan şükrün aksâmını câmi‘

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who know prayer's delight find tranquility in God's remembrance, which is the greatest remembrance; the Prophet said prayer was made the comfort of his eyes.
rows.anchor: أَلَا بِذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ ٱلْقُلُوبُ [er-Ra‘d 13/28], وَلَذِكْرُ ٱللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True prayer strips the heart of rival objects of worship; shirk violates the God-given human conscience, while Islam's essential meaning is sincere monotheistic surrender to God.
rows.anchor: İslâm’ın asıl mânası da bu ihlâs ile tevhiddir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer mixed with shirk or ostentation fails to give God His due and is the heedless prayer condemned in the preceding sura.
rows.anchor: evvelki sûrede geçtiği üzere namazlarından yanılmış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing the recipient as one specially related to his Lord expresses a particular lordship and servitude, honors the Prophet, and urges the command's fullest fulfillment.
rows.anchor: muhatabın ubûdiyet-i hâssasını ifade eder ki, bunda da ayrıca bir izhâr-ı tekrim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in li-rabbika marks entitlement or exclusive specification: pray sincerely for your Lord alone and turn toward Him in unity and devotion.
rows.anchor: mahza rubûbiyet hakkı olarak Allah için hulûs-i niyet ile kılınması lüzûmunu anlatmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author paraphrases the restriction as worshipping exclusively for the generous Lord, in contrast with polytheists, deniers, and show-offs.
rows.anchor: O hâlde sen o müşriklerin, mükezziblerin, mürâîlerin hilâfına olarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The special relation to the Lord displays honor and dignity, drawing the Prophet to carry out the command in its fullest form.
rows.anchor: emrin ekmel surette îfâsına bir sevk ü tergīb vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should worship sincerely, pray for his generous Lord, and sacrifice valuable living property, especially large camels, to feed people in need and publicly manifest divine generosity.
rows.anchor: mâ‘ûnu men‘edenlerin hilâfına fedâkârlık ederek kıymetli, canlı mallardan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because wa-nhar is joined to salli, li-rabbika governs both: prayer and slaughter count as worship only when sincerely for God; slaughter dedicated to another or without God's name is forbidden carrion.
rows.anchor: Allah için kesilmeyen de kurban olmaz. Kurban olmak şöyle dursun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coordinating waw requires combining prayer and sacrifice but does not require immediate sequence; a fā before nahr would have indicated that, though promptness may still be encouraged.
rows.anchor: öyle olsaydı فَانْحَرْ buyurulurdu. Ma‘amâfîh mümkin olduğu kadar tesrî‘inde nedbden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The familiar nahr day and the contrast with those withholding al-ma'un point to doing both acts: sincere bodily worship and financial generosity through sacrifice.
rows.anchor: mâ‘ûnu men‘edenlere tekabülü de bu iki emrin cem‘iyledir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sacrifice is an Abrahamic practice and a greater financial self-sacrifice than zakat or fitr charity; capacity is required, but the threshold is less demanding than zakat's.
rows.anchor: kurban kesmek, zekât ve sadaka-i fıtır vermekten daha fazla bir fedâkârlık ifade eden bir ibadettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salli here derives from salat meaning ritual prayer, not tasliya or merely supplication.
rows.anchor: bu صَلِّ emri namaz demek olan “salât”tandır, “tasliye”den ve sade dua mânasından değildir

rows.speaker: Ebû Müslim
rows.claim: He prefers taking salat as the prescribed obligatory prayers; Ibn Abbas is also reported to hold this view by Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir.
rows.anchor: Ebû Müslim salât-ı mektûbe, yani farz namazlar olmasını tercih eylemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This single command does not clearly establish every obligatory prayer, already established by other verses; interpreting it as simply continuing prayer makes it a reiteration unless it descended at the Mi'raj with the five prayers.
rows.anchor: Emrin vücub ifade etmesi bunda zâhir gibi görünürse de

rows.speaker: müfessirîn
rows.claim: Many interpreters take salat generically to include both obligatory and voluntary prayer, requiring every prayer to be sincerely for God; the obligation concerns its exclusive dedication, not the underlying act alone.
rows.anchor: Farzlara da nevâfile de şâmil cins-i salât denilmiştir. Çokları bunu tercih eylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although exclusive dedication to God is certainly conveyed by li-rabbika, the passage also appears to impose on the Prophet a thanksgiving prayer accompanied by sacrifice because of the gift and its placement against al-ma'un.
rows.anchor: bilhassa bir şükür namazı ile bir kurbanın vücûbunu da ifade eder

rows.speaker: müfessirîn
rows.claim: A further reported interpretation takes the prayer as the Eid prayer and nahr as the sacrificial animals offered at Eid al-Adha.
rows.anchor: bu namazdan murad bayram namazı, “nahr”dan murad da dahâyâ

rows.speaker: Mücâhid, Atâ ve İkrime
rows.claim: They are reported to interpret the prayer as the Eid-morning dawn prayer at Muzdalifa and nahr as the sacrifices made at Mina.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid, Atâ ve İkrime’den mervî olduğu üzere bir kısım müfessirîn de bu namazdan murad bayram

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both specific Eid interpretations are difficult because the sura is famously Meccan and Eid prayer is not known to have been performed in Mecca; the Mina view is further questionable because Hajj was not yet obligatory there.
rows.anchor: bu sûrenin nüzûlü Mekkî olduğuna göre bu iki mânanın tahsîsi de müşkildir

rows.speaker: Sa‘îd b. Cübeyr
rows.claim: He reports revelation at Hudaybiya: the Prophet delivered the Adha sermon, prayed two rak'as, then sacrificed; some use this to require prayer before slaughter or support two revelations.
rows.anchor: Sa‘îd b. Cübeyr’den bu âyetin Hudeybiye’de nâzil olduğuna

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Hudaybiya report is accepted, Kawthar would also allude to the treaty described as a manifest victory, but the report's authenticity is unestablished against the sura's famous Meccan dating.
rows.anchor: Hudeybiye sulhune bir işareti de tazammun etmiş olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command's obligation is specific to the Prophet, recipient of Kawthar: a thanksgiving and rejoicing prayer paired with public sacrifice and hospitality to the needy to display God's gift.
rows.anchor: Bu âyet ile sâbit olan vücub, Peygamber’e mahsustur, onun havâssındandır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This Meccan prayer, obligatory for the Prophet, most plausibly underlies later Eid prayer, particularly the Eid al-Adha prayer for those not at Hajj.
rows.anchor: bayram namazlarına ve bâhusus hacda bulunmayanlar hakkında kurban bayramı namazına esas olan bir namaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most suitable identification is the duha prayer, since tahajjud and duha were prescribed obligations for the Prophet beyond the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: buna da en yakışan kuşluk namazı olmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nahr command connects the prayer especially with Hajj's sacrificial days, while the teaching encourages continued obligatory and voluntary prayer and adds financial sacrifice to bodily worship.
rows.anchor: bunda farz namazlara devam ve hatta nâfileye de teşvik mânası bulunmakla beraber

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Mecca the Prophet maintained extra prayers beyond the five, including witr and duha, and sacrificed during nahr days and at other times even before Hajj was obligatory; he likely paired sacrifice with duha or thanksgiving prayer.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah Mekke’de iken dahi bu minval üzere hareket etmiş, beş vakit farz namazlardan mâ‘adâ daha

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Medina the Prophet established Eid prayer and sacrifice for the community by his own command and practice, rather than this verse directly prescribing them for everyone.
rows.anchor: ümmet için bu namaz ve kurbanın sübut ve takrîri doğrudan doğruya bu âyet ile değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some infer that eligible Muslims must sacrifice by following the Prophet's command, especially those who place the revelation in Medina.
rows.anchor: Medine’de nüzûlüne kāil olanlar buna zâhib olmuşlar ise de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Legal theory does not make the Prophet's acts that are exclusive to him binding on his followers; the hadith explicitly lists duha, udhiyah, and witr as obligations for him alone.
rows.anchor: Üç şey benim üzerime yazıldı (yani farz kılındı) sizin üzerinize yazılmadı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the Prophet's acts may be obligatory for him without being so for the community, these commands would be his sunnah for them unless another instruction or prohibition applied; uncertain contextual evidence may establish a practical wajib.
rows.anchor: Bunlar ümmet hakkında başkaca bir emir veya nehiy bulunmadıkça olsa olsa Peygamber’in sünneti olarak meşrû olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahmad and Ibn Majah transmit a warning that a person with means who does not sacrifice should not approach the Prophet's prayer place.
rows.anchor: İmam Ahmed ve İbn Mâce’nin rivayetleri üzere

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic command urges sacrifice because it is the practice of Abraham, the community's forefather.
rows.anchor: Bir de şu emr-i nebevî vardır: ضَحُّوا فَإِنـَّهَا سُنَّةُ أَبِيكُمْ إبـْرَاهِيم

rows.speaker: İbn Ömer
rows.claim: When asked whether udhiyah is obligatory, he replied that the Prophet and Muslims sacrificed; al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih and says scholars practice it as sunnah, not farz.
rows.anchor: ضَحَّى رَسُولُ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَالْمُسْلِمُونَ

rows.speaker: İbn Ömer
rows.claim: He reports that the Prophet lived in Medina for ten years and always offered udhiyah.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah Medine’de on sene ikāmet etti, hep udhiye kurbanı yapıyordu

rows.speaker: Berâ b. Âzib
rows.claim: He narrates the Prophet's rule not to slaughter until prayer: his uncle had slaughtered early to feed family and neighbors, so was told to slaughter again; a milk-fed goatling sufficed for him alone.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem bir nahr günü bize hutbede buyurdu ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The early-slaughter report is called hasan sahih and reflects the majority practice: towns with Friday and Eid prayer wait until the Imam's Eid prayer; some permit village sacrifice after dawn.
rows.anchor: ekser ehl-i ilim indinde amel bunun üzerinedir

rows.speaker: İbn Mübârek
rows.claim: He permits villagers who do not hold Eid prayer to sacrifice once dawn has risen; scholars say a young goat does not suffice, but a young sheep does, even at six or seven months.
rows.anchor: İbn Mübârek’in kavlidir ve bütün ehl-i ilim keçinin ceza‘ı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Post-prayer udhiyah is established through the Prophet's conduct and order: it was obligatory for him but not farz for the community, and he neither omitted it nor accepted sacrifice before Eid prayer.
rows.anchor: kurban bayramı namazından sonra kurban kesmek Resûlullah’ın fiil ve emriyle sâbit olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This enduring sunnah is a public religious rite and established practice close to farz; Hanafi usage calls a duty wajib when a threat and uncertain proof support it, meaning a quasi-obligation.
rows.anchor: dinde şe‘âirden olarak tarîkat-ı meslûke olmuş mânasına bir sünnettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa's apparent transmission considers udhiyah wajib; other scholars saying it is not wajib mean that it is not farz.
rows.anchor: İmâm-ı A‘zam’dan zâhir-i rivayette vâcibdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sacrifices required by vows and some Hajj rites are wajib, while aqiqah and other sacrifices for thanksgiving or charity are recommended voluntary acts; legal details belong in fiqh works.
rows.anchor: Nüzûr, hac nüsük ve şe‘âirinden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nahr is the noun for the upper chest or throat hollow and a verbal noun for striking or reaching that hollow, including inserting a knife there; because camels are cut there, it came to mean slaughter generally.
rows.anchor: Masdar olan “nahr” ise; Râgıb vesâir ehl-i lügatın beyânına göre aslında nahra isabet ettirmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intihar derives from nahr; zabh can be done by cutting below the jaw, while wa-nhar comes from the verbal noun nahr and plainly means slaughter.
rows.anchor: “İntihar” da bundan me’huzdur. Sûre-i Mâide’de geçtiği üzere mâlum ki “zebh”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though slaughter can be for food or sale, the worship-and-gratitude context and familiar name for the days of Eid sacrifice make the sacrificial meaning clear, including celebrating Eid.
rows.anchor: burada sevk-i kelâm şükür ve ibadet mânası üzerinde olduğu için de kurban mânası zâhirdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted object leaves nahr's animal unspecified: perform the rite or shed blood for God of any important animal fit for sacrifice, with the act rather than one species intended.
rows.anchor: Fakat وَانْحَرْ emrinin mef‘ûlü zikredilmemiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most commentators supply wa-nhar al-budn because Arab usage especially associates nahr with camels and Qur'an 22:36 names sacrificial camels; the intent is exemplary large valuable victims, not camel-only sacrifice.
rows.anchor: Arabın örfünde “nahr” deve kesmekte gālib olduğu

rows.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
rows.claim: In al-Bahr he says the majority mean Hajj offerings, rites, and udhiyah by nahr; with no jihad then, prayer and sacrifice were commanded together.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hayyân Bahr’da der ki: “‘Nahr’dan murad hedy, nüsük, dahâyâ nahrıdır

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: He likewise says the majority intend udhiyah sacrifice; the author notes that his wording appears to restrict the command to udhiyah, in accord with the hadith about the Prophet's special obligations.
rows.anchor: Âlûsi de ekseriyetin dahâyâ nahrı murad olması üzerinde olduğunu söylemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In legal terminology nahr is clear as slaughter but leaves its object ambiguous; prophetic practice identifies the eight male and female sheep, goats, camels, and cattle as valid large sacrifices.
rows.anchor: “nahr” boğazlamak mânasında zâhirdir, fakat mef‘ûlü hakkında mücmeldir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The camel-associated word signals attention to substantial, valuable, excellent offerings and to nahr days; sheep is the most general sacrificial threshold and is better in quality, while a ram is called the best sacrifice.
rows.anchor: “nahr” devede daha mâruf olmakla beraber diğerlerinin de nahr şânındandır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A well-known report says the Prophet personally slaughtered two handsome horned rams, naming God, magnifying Him, and putting his foot on their sides.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah’ın udhiyesinde boynuzlu güzel iki koçu بِسْمِ اللهِ وَاللهُ أَكْبَر diyerek

rows.speaker: Câbir
rows.claim: He says that after the Adha prayer and sermon the Prophet slaughtered a ram for himself and for community members unable to sacrifice.
rows.anchor: Câbir radıyallahu anh’tan rivayet edildiği üzere de demiştir ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A camel or cow may be shared by seven; one person's whole offering is more meritorious, but their young do not suffice. Other vowed, charitable, or thanksgiving sacrifices may use any edible animal at any time.
rows.anchor: Deve ve sığır cinsi bedenelerin yedi kişiye kurban olabileceği de beyan buyurulmuştur

rows.speaker: Ebu’l-Ahvas
rows.claim: Against the majority, he interprets wa-nhar as facing the chest toward the qibla.
rows.anchor: İbn Ebî Hâtim’in rivayetine göre Ebu’l-Ahvas

rows.speaker: Ferrâ
rows.claim: He also adopts the facing interpretation, explaining tanahur as reciprocal facing and citing a line about opposing homes or valleys.
rows.anchor: Ferrâ da buna zâhib olmuş ve tevilinde şöyle demiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although tanahur can mean facing one another, leaving the familiar slaughter sense for a metaphor built on another metaphor to mean facing the qibla is unsound; if it meant confrontation, close combat would fit better.
rows.anchor: mâruf olan mânayı bırakıp da mecaz üstüne mecaz olarak kıbleye istikbâl mânasını anlamaya kalkışmak doğru olmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report from Ali says Gabriel explained nahr as raising hands at the opening takbir and at bowing, a practice of the angels and prayer's adornment; al-Suyuti calls its chain weak, Ibn Kathir very munkar, and Ibn al-Jawzi fabricated.
rows.anchor: Suyûtî bunun senedine zayıf demiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports from Abu Ja'far, Ali, Anas, and Ibn Abbas concern lifting hands at prayer's opening or placing the right hand over the left at the chest; their authenticity is not established, though al-Suyuti finds one Ali chain acceptable.
rows.anchor: bunların da sıhhati sâbit olamamıştır

rows.speaker: Dahhâk, Süleyman-ı Teymî
rows.claim: They are also reported to recommend raising the hands to the chest in supplication after prayer.
rows.anchor: Dahhâk ile Süleyman-ı Teymî de “namazdan sonra duada ellerini göğsüne kaldır” demiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These reports might concern people unable to sacrifice or prayer etiquette, but cannot replace nahr's well-known meaning of sacrifice or fold it into salli; all are merely prayer practices.
rows.anchor: “nahr”ın mâlum ve meşhur olan kurban kesmek mânasını bırakıp âyeti bunlarla tevile kalkışmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prayer-only interpretation would command sincerity against show-offs but omit the aid and generosity demanded by al-ma'un, making it disproportionate to gratitude for Kawthar.
rows.anchor: Allah için halka mu‘âvenet olan bir hayır ve kerem fazl u faziletini ihtivâ etmiş olmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clearest meaning is sincere prayer plus valuable sacrifice for God, greater self-denial than zakat, and generous assistance to God's servants as bodily and financial thanksgiving for Kawthar.
rows.anchor: kurban keserek zekâttan dahi fazla bir fedâkârlıkla kıymetli mallara kıyıp

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once this main sense is established, further possible allusions may be appreciated according to taste and insight.
rows.anchor: bundan mümkin ve muhtemil olabilen diğer birtakım işaretler daha anlamakta ise zevk ve irfan için hacr yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author renders wa-nhar as sacrifice rather than merely slaughter, taking the command as a practical enactment of the commands in al-An'am and al-Duha to dedicate worship and proclaim God's blessings.
rows.anchor: meâlde “kurban kesmek” tâbiriyle ifadeyi “boğazla” demekten daha muvâfık bulduk

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gift calls for wholehearted gratitude in heart, speech, body, and wealth: pray sincerely, sacrifice, worship in unity, serve others, and proclaim God's favor; the Prophet's gift cannot be cut off.
rows.anchor: namaz kıl, namaz kılmakla beraber kurban da kes, O’na böyle tevhid ve ihlâs ile fedâkârâne ibadet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shani' means anyone who persistently hates the Prophet; that person alone is abtar, cut off from future, descendants, good name, and reputation, while the Prophet's followers, religion, book, legacy, and reward endure.
rows.anchor: senin şâni’in sana şeneânı olan; buğz, kin tutan, hınç besleyen her kim olursa olsun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A shani' is an active participle from shana'an, hatred as in al-Ma'ida 5:8; it denotes fixed persistence rather than a past episode, so those who later repent and believe are excluded.
rows.anchor: zaman ve hudûs mânası değil, devam ve sübût mânası maksuddur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abtar is a descriptive adjective, not a comparative, from cutting; its feminine is batra, and ordinary usage describes a severed tail, yielding the Turkish sense stump or truncated.
rows.anchor: “Ebter” uyûbdan olduğu için ef‘al-i tafdîl değil, sıfat-ı müşebbehedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the tail is at the rear, abtar metaphorically means one without descendants or lasting effect, or an unfinished undertaking without a good outcome; the hadith applies it to important work not begun in God's name.
rows.anchor: sonunda arkası olmayan, yani zürriyeti olmayan, kendinden sonra eseri kalmayan kimselere

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith's abtar means an important undertaking lacks a good completion and remains incomplete if it is not begun in God's name; all things perish except God's face.
rows.anchor: “Ehemmiyetli olan herhangi bir iş Allah’ın ismiyle başlanmazsa o iş ebterdir” hadîsinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite predicate in the restrictive sentence makes abtar exclusive to the hater, negating every form of cut-offness from the Prophet and assigning all its possible senses to his enemy, especially the one taunting him after his son's death.
rows.anchor: cümle kasr ifade ettiğinden dolayı ebterlik mefhûmunu Peygamber’den külliyen nefy ile ona buğz edene hasrettiği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction confirms that the recipient of unending abundant good cannot be cut off, while every hater is truly truncated; this general causal proof, a rhetorical madhhab kalami, also foretells the named mocker's ruin.
rows.anchor: haber verilmekle ebter diyen kâfirin ebterliğini de bilhassa haber vermiş bulunuyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some restrict the occasion of revelation to As ibn Wa'il, Abu Jahl, a Quraysh group, or Ka'b ibn Ashraf, but the derived description of a hater is general and the author says all who hated the Prophet became abtar.
rows.anchor: Âs b. Vâil veya Ebû Cehil veya Kureyş’ten bir cemaat veya Ka‘b b. Eşref

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's haters were cut off materially in lineage or spiritually in good works and remembrance, and passed away disgraced; any descendants who embraced Islam became the Prophet's community and spiritual children.
rows.anchor: Ya maddeten nesl ü nesebi veya mânen hayr u zikri kesilmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslim descendants cannot benefit unbelieving ancestors through prayer or intercession, while unrighteous unbelieving descendants are no good successors; the unbelievers' own prayers go futilely astray.
rows.anchor: mânevî evlâdı olmuşlar, مَا كَانَ لِلنَّبِىِّ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ أَن يَسْتَغْفِرُوا۟ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ
